links.outcome: Association between nurse engagement with SHAP explanations and satisfaction
links.effect: 82 of 156 nurses (52.6%) regularly engaged with SHAP; engagement positively associated with satisfaction (Pearson r=0.456; P<.001)
links.quote: Among 156 nurses, 82 (52.6%) regularly engaged with Shapley Additive Explanations; this engagement was positively associated with satisfaction (Pearson r=0.456; P<.001).

links.outcome: Fairness metrics across nurse experience tiers before versus after AI-assisted scheduling
links.effect: Workload CV decreased 50% (0.18-0.09; P<.001); disparate impact ratios normalized from 1.35-1.56 to 1.01-1.04; preference satisfaction equity across experience tiers (ANOVA P=.38)
links.quote: Preexisting experience-based bias was fully eliminated: workload coefficient of variation (CV) decreased 50% (0.18-0.09; P<.001), disparate impact ratios normalized from 1.35-1.56 to 1.01-1.04, and preference satisfaction equity was achieved across experience tiers (ANOVA P=.38).

unlisted_practices: Fairness-audited AI nurse scheduling with weight sensitivity analysis
AI-assisted workforce scheduling to reduce administrative burden

screen.reason: Evaluates a real-world pre-post deployment of an explainable AI and fairness-audited nurse scheduling system in a hospital setting, specifically assessing the impact of fairness auditing and SHAP-based explainability interfaces on staff satisfaction, scheduling time, and bias.
